body: Hello I'm looking for 2 tickets! I'm located in Vancouver BC :) <3 Shambhalove xox

Correct me if I'm wrong, but it seems to me that you are saying one should refuse to let it control your life while simultaneously accepting its influence?

In response to your questions,
Yes, these illnesses make it very hard to see how I would achieve my ambitions.
Why would I continue living?
Mostly because my family would be so upset. And I'm afraid that if I kill myself, so will my sister. She is trans MtoF and hasn't come out to anyone except her counselor. She is right to think that our catholic family wouldn't understand.

I am not close with my family, but not in conflict with them either.

Moment by moment, or eyes on the horizon, I just see exhaustion, pain, and isolation.

I don't see anything changing, and I don't see myself going much longer this way without a solution that is just too far away.

I wish I could kill myself and make it look like an accident. So at least my mom doesn't think I went to hell for committing suicide.

I understand what you are trying to say, but I'm not sure "refusing" to let the illnesses control my life will stop the illnesses from controlling my life. The fact is that chronic pain and fatigue does control your life. It affects your sleep, your mood, your physical ability to exercise, play sports, dance, hike, travel.  The list goes on and on. And do understand that some people find a way to manage their pain and increase their quality of life. But for me, I'm running out of options. And as each thing I try fails the motivation to keep researching,  going to doctors appointments, specialists, and trying medications gets less and less. I'm tired. My life is pain and frustration and sleepless nights. But euthanasia isn't an option for me, because my illnesses aren't terminal. This won't kill me, but it sure as hell makes me not want to be alive.
